findings.statement: CA9, first in the convergence ranking, is held almost entirely by malignant RCC cells [gene=CA9; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.976].
Paired by donor, CA9 is far higher in RCC tumour cells than in normal proximal tubule cells (the cell of origin), so the bulk signal is tumour-intrinsic and not stromal.

In Visium, the spots with high CA9 are surrounded by RCC spots (significant neighbour enrichment) and RCC explains nearly all of the composition-corrected CA9 signal. Macrophage neighbours are only weakly enriched.

The AlphaFold CA9 model is of moderate overall confidence [gene=CA9; type=alphafold_model; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; mean_plddt=76.56], and its top detected cavity gives a moderate structural-context score [gene=CA9; type=structural_context; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; structural_context_score=0.546]. This is a descriptive heuristic only, not a degron or ligase prediction. Cavity detection recovers about half of the experimental ligand-contact residues [gene=CA9; type=ligand_site_validation; source=PDBe-KB ligand sites (experimental holo structures); recall=0.5].

MET is held mainly by RCC tumour cells [gene=MET; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.935], with endothelium contributing a minor share. This makes it a tumour-cell receptor target.

KDR is an endothelial gene [gene=KDR; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Endothelial; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.951], and Visium shows it in endothelium and not in RCC cells. It is a microenvironment (anti-angiogenic) target, not a tumour-cell target.

EPAS1 (HIF-2 alpha) transcripts in the scRNA-seq are mostly endothelial and fibroblast. RCC cells hold only a small share, so bulk EPAS1 signal should not be read as tumour-cell expression, although droplet dropout limits this reading. The protein is nonetheless the drug target through its activity.
CD74 is expressed at very high levels in antigen-presenting cells (dendritic cells, macrophages, B cells). It is a microenvironment target and not a tumour-cell target.
CXCR4 is expressed by lymphocytes (CD4 T, B, CD8 T and regulatory T cells), so the bulk signal reflects infiltrating immune cells and not RCC cells.

COL23A1, a transmembrane collagen, leads the tumour track and is made mainly by RCC cells [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.881]. It has few ccRCC papers and no clinical drug. It is strongly higher in TCGA tumours [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; tcga_log2fc=5.829], the rise survives extrapolation to a pure tumour [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; rna_lfc_at_purity1=4.88], and it is not associated with adverse survival. Missing before validation: no selective DepMap dependency, unconfirmed protein localisation and normal-tissue staining, expression in only a minority of RCC cells, and a literature count made by gene symbol.

The AlphaFold model of COL23A1 is low-confidence [gene=COL23A1; type=alphafold_model; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; mean_plddt=58.91], with only one tiny, shallow cavity. The structure gives little support for a small-molecule approach, and an antibody against the extracellular domain is the more plausible route.

RAB42, a small Rab GTPase in the tumour track, is carried mainly by RCC cells [gene=RAB42; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.627]. It replicates in TCGA and holds at full purity [gene=RAB42; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; rna_lfc_at_purity1=3.189], with few ccRCC papers and no clinical drug. Caveats: it has no dependency evidence, and a small GTPase is mostly intracellular, so the surface-or-secreted tractability flag is doubtful.

OLFML2A leads the stroma track and is a fibroblast gene [gene=OLFML2A; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=stroma; source_share=0.647]. It replicates in TCGA, holds at full purity [gene=OLFML2A; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=stroma; rna_lfc_at_purity1=1.527] and is not linked to adverse prognosis. It is a stromal target, not a tumour-cell target. Missing: dependency evidence, and it is expressed in colon (vital-organ check).

COX4I2 (stroma track) is attributed to fibroblasts [gene=COX4I2; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=stroma; source_share=0.893]. It has few ccRCC papers, no clinical drug and no adverse survival association. A mitochondrial subunit is a poor antibody target, so the surface flag needs checking, and lung expression is relatively high.

GAL3ST4 leads the immune track and is held by macrophages [gene=GAL3ST4; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=immune; source_share=0.972]. It replicates in TCGA, but its bulk rise shrinks markedly at full purity [gene=GAL3ST4; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=immune; rna_lfc_at_purity1=0.401], and higher expression goes with worse survival [gene=GAL3ST4; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=immune; tcga_cox_log_hr=0.177]. There is only one ccRCC paper. The effect is macrophage-specific and not shown to be causal.

The AlphaFold GAL3ST4 model is reasonably confident [gene=GAL3ST4; type=alphafold_model; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; mean_plddt=79.31] and has the highest structural-context score among the candidates examined [gene=GAL3ST4; type=structural_context; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; structural_context_score=0.7874]. This is a descriptive monomer heuristic only and does not identify degrons or predict degradation.

LILRB4 (immune track) is a macrophage gene. The screen flags its bulk upregulation as infiltration-driven and not purity-robust, so it is a macrophage-checkpoint hypothesis and not a tumour-intrinsic one.

GBP5 (immune track) comes mostly from CD8 T cells. It is flagged infiltration-driven and not purity-robust, with an adverse-survival flag, so it marks T-cell infiltration and is not a tumour-cell target.

caveats: ALDOB, SLC22A8, CD70, SCARB1, PIGR, NNMT, EGFR and others from the convergence ranking were not profiled at the cell level for lack of tool budget. CD70 was queried, but it is not cited because its single-cell records carry no evidence id.
Single-cell share of transcripts depends on how many cells of each type were captured; endothelium and fibroblasts are sparse.
Discovery candidates are data-ranked hypotheses. None has a selective DepMap dependency or functional evidence, and literature is counted by gene symbol.
Structural-context scores are monomer heuristics and do not identify degrons, ligase compatibility or degradation. Low-confidence models (COL23A1) cannot support pocket conclusions.
